article_title: AI-based Verbal and Visual Scaffolding in a Serious Game: Effects on Learning and Cognitive Load
citation: Caroline Wermann, Karina E. Avila, Sebastian André, Julia C. Draeger, Alvar Goetze, Jochen Kuhn, Maite Maurer, Sascha Mehlhase, Nikola Merkas, Fabian Schrodt, and Stefan Küchemann. (2026). AI-based Verbal and Visual Scaffolding in a Serious Game: Effects on Learning and Cognitive Load. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08893
title: Qookies' seven pedagogical design principles for AI-scaffolded serious games
description: The article enumerates seven design foundations integrated into Qookies: personalization (adaptable and adaptive), verbal and visual scaffolding via an AI NPC, ICAP-based engagement, minimization of extraneous cognitive load, serious-game framing around escape-room levels, multiple external representations, and collaborative knowledge construction. The authors state that "in the current study, only aspects 1 to 3 are manipulated between conditions" while the rest are identical across conditions.
requirements: Learning-irrelevant objects must not exhibit colorful contrast or be manipulable, to avoid raising extraneous cognitive load
constraints: Only personalization, scaffolding, and ICAP were manipulated between conditions; the other mechanisms were implemented identically across conditions
target_learners: general public without prior physics or mathematics knowledge
target_learning_goals: conceptual and procedural understanding through puzzle solving
examples: Players adjust a qubit's state on a Bloch sphere to solve levels; verbal scaffolding via a Llama 3.1 70B chatbot prompted with level concepts but not solutions

title: Qookies serious game for quantum technology concepts
description: Qookies is a theory-based serious game designed to make abstract quantum technology concepts accessible to learners without prior mathematics or physics knowledge. Learners "progress through the game by solving interactive educational puzzles" complemented by short conceptual units in simple language, framed as escape-room-based levels. It targets a heterogeneous audience including school students, university students, and the general public.
requirements: Content must be introduced in an intuitive, visual, and experiential way given the heterogeneous audience
constraints: The perceived goal for learners is solving escape-room levels, not explicit academic learning
target_learning_goals: fundamental quantum technology concepts such as qubits, superposition, and the Bloch sphere
examples: A 25-minute gameplay session with 16-item pre/post concept tests produced significant gains in all conditions

title: AI NPC architecture combining reinforcement learning and an LLM via an embodiment interface
description: The game's non-player character is controlled by two AI models: a generative chatbot (Llama 3.1 70B) prompted with the level's underlying concepts but not its solution, and a visual scaffolding model based on one-shot reinforcement learning. The architecture "combines reinforcement learning and a large language model via an embodiment interface, grounding dialogue and action generation in the current game state", which the authors state reduces hallucination risk and keeps dialogue aligned with game mechanics.
requirements: The reinforcement learning component is initialized without prior task-specific knowledge and learns from gameplay observation, so it cannot help in new situations
constraints: Because the action AI must first learn from the player, it cannot help in new situations, which the authors note may discourage first-time users
target_learning_goals: quantum technology concepts supported through verbal explanation and visual action demonstration
examples: The NPC offers a 'Talk to' chat menu for verbal scaffolding and a 'Do something' menu through which the AI performs in-game actions
